codeReview.summary: Fail with one blocking issue. The feature completes first-class `flux apps register`, `update`, `register-and-verify`, `update-and-verify`, `wait-propagation`, and `messages` wiring, reuses planning artifacts, and adds focused contract tests for auth, confirm, and propagation states. However, the CLI does not actually preserve the explicit `error` status for all verify-flow failures, so VAL-APPS-008 and VAL-CROSS-006 are not fully satisfied.

issues.description: `handleAppsVerifyFlowCommand` converts thrown MCP failures into a generic `emitFailure(classifyFailureKind(message), ...)` response before the payload can preserve `summary.status` (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:7128-7130`, compare the later payload shaping at `fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:7134-7152`). The upstream MCP verify tools can throw before returning structured content when the submission response has no extractable hash (`flux-mcp/src/index.ts:8803-8806` and `flux-mcp/src/index.ts:9509-9512`). In that path the CLI returns `status: "flux_error"` instead of the explicit verify-flow `status: "error"` required by VAL-APPS-008. The added regression only stubs a structured `{ ok: false, status: "error" }` result (`fluxos-cli/test/apps-submit-propagation.test.ts:945-1004`), so it misses this real MCP error path.

sharedStateObservations.observation: There is still no shared guidance/source of truth for how first-class CLI commands should preserve MCP business-status values when a tool throws before returning structured content.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/library/shared-runtime.md` notes that failure classification is not yet shared; this feature drift shows the practical gap via `fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:7128-7130` versus the MCP verify-tool throw sites at `flux-mcp/src/index.ts:8803-8806` and `flux-mcp/src/index.ts:9509-9512`.
